transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2025-12-23
- Start: 10:00 AM PST
- Duration: ~45 minutes
- Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Samira (Redwood SE), Liam (Acme Head of AI), Priya (Acme ML Eng), Daniel (Acme Security)

Summary: (auto) Quick review of weekly quality evals, notes on regression and guardrails, agree on follow-ups and timeline for canary. Some transcription artifacts expected.

00:00 Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. this is our weekly POC sync for the Acme pilot. Samira and I are here from Redwood. how's everyone doing?
00:08 Liam: Good thanks, quick morning for us. excited to see the results you sent yesterday.
00:12 Priya: hi all, I pulled the spreadsheet, gonna be a few questions during the deep dive.
00:18 Samira: Great, we'll walk through the eval summary first then dig into the failing prompt buckets and guardrail suggestions.
01:05 Jordan: Quick agenda  - 1) eval highlights 2) regression items 3) guardrail updates 4) next steps. Sound ok?
01:12 Liam: yep

03:10 Samira: Ok slide one, overall accuracy and answer quality. On the primary prompt set the model (redwood-curie-v2  - note: transcription may call it curie) scored 87% pass rate on the acceptance criteria, which aligns with last week at a high level, but there are pockets of regressions when we added the new edge-case prompts.
03:32 Priya: Right the new edge-cases bumped false-positives for the compliance detection heuristics. We saw more hallucinations around regulatory citations.
03:40 Samira: Exactly. We profiled the errors  - around 14% of failing items relate to hallucinated citations, 6% are formatting issues, and 3% are policy-misaligned. The rest are low-confidence truncations.
04:05 Daniel: On the security side I'm more concerned with any data leakage or PII exposures. Did the eval flag any potential PII?
04:15 Samira: We have a PII detector that ran and flagged two examples  - both were due to the prompt including a sample log line from production; we'll mark those as prompt contamination. Not a model leakage but we should scrub prompts.

06:00 Jordan: On scoring, we're using a hybrid of automated heuristics plus manual spot checks. The spreadsheet includes columns for intent match, factuality, and guardrail flags. It's possible you'll see some rows where the auto label is aggressive.
06:25 Priya: can you remind us of the threshold for acceptance? last doc said 90% overall but we agreed to 85% for pilot.
06:33 Jordan: Right  - pilot acceptance is 85% pass-rate; goal for production is 90+. For the canary we want minimum 87 on the trimmed prompt set.

09:10 Samira: Regression specifics  - when we merged the new prompt variants (edge-case-1..5) we saw a 4 point drop on average. The top failing buckets: regulatory-citation hallucinations, ambiguous entity resolution, and prompt-formatting that caused melted JSON output.
09:35 Priya: melted JSON? yeah some outputs had bracket mismatch, likely tokenization or truncation.
09:45 Samira: We believe that's due to the sequence length and an unescaped user example in a prompt template  - easy fix by sanitizing examples and increasing the stop token heuristics.

12:00 Jordan: For guardrails we proposed two changes: 1) tighter citation policy  - prefer quoting from allowed sources, 2) add a post-generation filter to mask/reject PII, and 3) a length/format validator to enforce strict JSON schema.
12:30 Daniel: For the KMS question  - if we use Redwood Private for dedicated trial, can we bring our keys or do you provision them?
12:42 Jordan: You can bring your KMS keys for Private; for Dedicated we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integration. We'll send the security integration guide.

15:05 Samira: We re-ran a focused eval after applying the first set of guardrails in sandbox. That reduced hallucinated citations by ~60% on the test subset but some edge-case prompts still fail. I've noted examples in the sheet prefixed FAIL-EDGE.
15:28 Priya: can you share which examples? I'm worried some are core to our user workflow.
15:35 Samira: Yep  - FAIL-EDGE-03, -07, -11 are ones where the model invents a regulation number. For those we suggest either prompt rewrite to avoid open-ended ask for citations or a retrieval augmentation if you need exact regs.
16:10 Liam: Retrieval would be fine but adds infra. cost and latency. tradeoff there.
16:20 Jordan: Right we discussed routing earlier  - for high-assurance requests we can route to a retrieval-equipped model variant or a more conservative smaller model with higher factuality but higher cost. We can test both in the POC.

19:00 Priya: what's the latency impact for retrieval? ballpark numbers?
19:10 Samira: For our internal benchmarks retrieval adds ~120-250ms per request depending on vector DB and cache hit rate. If you run in Dedicated with local vectors it's toward 120ms.
19:28 Priya: that's acceptable for batch workflows but makes interactive checks trickier.

21:00 Jordan: On the scoring methodology  - we added a 'regression severity' tag (low/med/high) for failing rows. High means user-visible incorrectness, medium is formatting, low is preference differences. We prioritize high for fixes.
21:25 Liam: how many high-severity failures?
21:30 Samira: Today there are 11 high, 26 medium, 18 low in the recent run (post-guardrail). The 11 high are mostly the citation/regulation hallucination cluster.

24:00 Priya: For the prompt set changes, can you show the before/after prompt text so we understand the rewrite?
24:08 Samira: Sure  - open the sheet. Example: original prompt: "List relevant regs with citations"  - rewrite: "Identify applicable regulations from the given corpus; do not invent regulation numbers; if unsure, respond: 'reference required'". That small change alone dropped hallucination on that example.

27:00 Daniel: On audit logs  - we need full token-level logs for a subset of calls for compliance. Is that available in the pilot?
27:10 Jordan: Yes  - in Dedicated and Private we can enable token-level logging and route logs to your S3 with encryption. For hosted we keep aggregated logs; token-level is available under enterprise add-on. We'll share the setup steps.

29:30 Samira: We also tested automated guardrail fallback  - if the model produces a citation flagged as untrusted it triggers a 'safe-fail' template that apologizes and recommends retrieval. That reduced user-facing hallucinations across the sample set.
29:50 Priya: Nice  - any user-facing changes we should expect? phrasing or longer replies?
30:00 Samira: Slightly longer in the safe-fail path but clearer and safer. We can tune verbosity.

33:00 Jordan: Let's go over timeline and next steps. We recommend: 1) Acme provides 20 more labeled edge-case examples by Friday 12/28, 2) Redwood re-runs regression with the updated guardrails by 12/26, 3) if passes, schedule a controlled canary week of 1/5 with production-like traffic and monitoring, 4) we share pricing and dedicated trial terms by 12/24.
33:40 Liam: That timeline works for us, pending legal on the trial terms.
33:46 Daniel: I'll review the SOC artifacts and KMS policy and aim to respond by 12/27.

36:00 Priya: A few quick questions  - can we toggle the post-filtering off in real-time? we might want to A/B test user experience.
36:10 Samira: Yes, we can expose the filter as a per-route flag in the config. You can turn it on/off and capture metrics. We'll add that to the demo next week.

38:00 Jordan: Any competitive concerns? I know you were also talking to Anthropic  - do you want us to highlight differences here?
38:12 Liam: Anthropic's approach seemed stricter on safety but heavier on latency. OpenAI had strong conversational quality but costs were a factor. It's not closed yet.

40:00 Jordan: Great. Quick recap of action items  - I've put them in the sheet but high level: pricing/terms, regression re-run, extra labeled prompts, security doc exchange, schedule canary. Anything to add?
40:20 Priya: please include the exact format for the labeled examples (CSV columns).
40:25 Samira: Will do  - I'll attach a template with two example rows.

42:00 Liam: Ok that's all from me, thanks to Jordan and Samira.
42:05 Jordan: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email and update the sheet. Talk soon.
42:12 Meeting end.

Notes about transcript quality: occasional speaker mislabels and some product names transcribed imprecisely (e.g., "redwood-curie-v2" might be mis-typed). The sheet links referenced: https://redwood.app/sheets/acme-poc-evals (note: placeholder link).
